experiment: Skip call-site heap inference for annotated local lambdas
hypothesis: Local lambda call-site inference only fills absent annotations. An early return for fully annotated or nullary lambdas removes a scope walk and unused call tables while recursive elaboration still visits their bodies.
correctness_counterexamples: Nullary and fully annotated local lambdas allocate no call-site inference table
Both ELet and ELetRec retain exact explicit annotations
Mixed annotated/unannotated parameters still infer heap arguments
Unannotated inner lambdas inside annotated outer lambdas are still elaborated

inference_extra_heap_growth_bytes.comparison: Elaboration with an annotated/nullary local lambda minus the same continuation with a non-lambda binding; 128 calls, AST construction excluded
inference_extra_heap_growth_bytes.note: The budget includes fixed AST rewrite costs and RC free-list reuse. RC heap-pointer growth does not measure total allocation volume. Both baselines fail the 512-byte budget; bump, RC and RC-shadow candidates pass.

interpretation: The comparison is a pure compiler implementation change: every generated target is byte-identical across compilers, temperatures and rounds. Heap-pointer, linear capacity and RSS are distinct metrics. Wall-time spread and the A/A control limit the precision of timing claims.
